explain.say: Your heart pounds when a car zooms past, and it also pounds before you sing on stage. Same feeling, but is it the same thing? Look at the two sides on the board: real danger, and scary but safe.

explain.say: So be a fear detective. Notice the fear, then ask the key question lighting up here: is this a real danger? If yes, move away and tell a grown-up. If no, breathe and take a small brave step. Can you sort your own fears this way?

explain.say: When something is scary but safe, facing it in small steps makes the fear shrink. Being brave does not mean not feeling scared; it means feeling scared and trying anyway. Well done! Challenge: pick one small scary-but-safe thing to try this week.

faq.q: What should I do in real danger?
faq.a: Move away from the danger, shout for help and tell a trusted grown-up. In an emergency, a grown-up can phone the emergency number, such as 112, 999 or 911, depending on your country.
asks: What do I do if I am in danger?

faq.q: Why am I scared of things that are safe?
faq.a: Your brain's alarm is extra careful, so it sometimes rings for things that only look or feel risky, like the dark or a spider. It would rather be safe than sorry.
asks: Why do I have silly fears?

faq.q: How can I tell if something is really dangerous?
faq.a: Ask: could this truly hurt me right now? Is there a trusted grown-up who says it is safe? If you are not sure, it is always fine to move away and ask a grown-up.
asks: Is this dangerous or just scary?

faq.q: Is it okay to be scared of the dark?
faq.a: Yes, it is one of the most common fears, and most children grow out of it. A night light, a cuddly toy or a calm breathing game at bedtime can help.
asks: Why am I afraid of the dark?

faq.a: Being brave means feeling scared and doing the right thing anyway. Even firefighters and astronauts feel fear; they have just practised facing it.

facts: Being afraid of the dark is one of the most common childhood fears, and most children grow out of it.
Scientists know of more than 50,000 kinds of spider, and only a tiny number are dangerous to people.
